title: How Zach Yadegari built Cal AI to $30M by 18 and treats college like a vacation
summary: Fortune profile of Zach Yadegari (18), who built the Cal AI calorie-tracking app to roughly $30M a year. Covers building from a personal pain point, TikTok and influencer-led growth, selling an earlier site for $100K, and why he still goes to college while rejecting the standard path.

principles.text: Build the product you personally wished existed; a bad experience with an incumbent is the idea.
principles.quote: For a kid, I was in school, that just wasn't sustainable

principles.text: Early distribution was short-form video plus influencer partnerships, which drove explosive growth.
principles.quote: We started making TikToks, we started partnering with influencers, and then we had pretty explosive growth

principles.text: Start with free products to build audience; monetize later with ads, then sell and move on to the next build.
principles.quote: I sold it when I was 16 for $100,000—and that’s when I started building apps.

principles.text: Reject the one-size-fits-all formula for success and choose your own path.
principles.quote: I’ve always been against the idea that everyone should follow the same formula: get good grades, go to a good college, get a degree, get a job, and then start making money.

principles.text: Surround yourself with other builders; use college for exploration and community, not direct business gain.
principles.quote: I look at it as I’m paying $100,000 a year for a vacation,

principles.text: Turn your builder network into a content brand that teaches others how to build apps.
principles.quote: We’re basically trying to lead the forefront of Gen Z builders,
